problem: The block reads "...y₂₂ = z₁₁/Δz, where Δz = z₁₁z₂₂ − z₁₂z₂₁ where: Δz is the determinant of the Z matrix, in Ω²." The word "where" appears twice in a row, which reads as a typo and breaks the otherwise clean formula-then-glossary pattern used in Sections 1 and 2.
fix: Write it once: "y₁₁ = z₂₂/Δz, y₁₂ = −z₁₂/Δz, y₂₁ = −z₂₁/Δz, y₂₂ = z₁₁/Δz, where Δz = z₁₁z₂₂ − z₁₂z₂₁ is the determinant of the Z matrix, in Ω². Each y comes out in S."

problem: "A passive T network of ordinary elements never hits this" is too strong. It is true only for networks of positive resistors. A passive lossless LC T network does reach Δz = 0 at a particular frequency: with Z₁ = Z₂ = jωL and Z₃ = 1/(jωC), Δz = −ω²L² + 2L/C, which is zero at ω = √(2/(LC)). At that frequency the input impedance with port 2 shorted is zero, so y₁₁ is infinite and no finite Y matrix exists, although the Z matrix is still finite.
fix: "A passive T network of positive resistors never hits this, because Δz = R₁R₂ + R₁R₃ + R₂R₃ > 0. Lossless LC networks can reach Δz = 0 at some frequencies, where a port short makes the input admittance infinite. An ideal transformer is the other classic case: ..."
